evidence: 'How I Could Just Kill a Man' (1991), produced by DJ Muggs, loops a guitar lick from the Jimi Hendrix Experience's 'Are You Experienced?' (1967), among other sources, as recorded in the song's sample credits.

later.title: How I Could Just Kill a Man

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Are You Experienced?' is full of sounds played backwards on tape: guitar and drums that swell up and cut off where they'd normally ring out. Muggs lifts a short guitar lick from it and loops it under B-Real's high voice and his own murky drums. Listen for Hendrix's guitar turned into a repeating pattern, a piece of 1967 psychedelia working as a hook in a 1991 rap single.

explanation.age7: Cypress Hill used a short piece of Jimi Hendrix's guitar in one of their first songs.
explanation.age13: Jimi Hendrix's 'Are You Experienced?' is full of guitar sounds recorded backwards. DJ Muggs took a short guitar lick from it and looped it for Cypress Hill's first single, 'How I Could Just Kill a Man'.
explanation.adult: Cross-lineage from rock into hip-hop, via the same producer who carries edges from Sly Stone and his own squeal. Muggs's crate evidently ran through psychedelic rock as much as funk.
